reason: This passage (Exodus 14) depicts a divinely-orchestrated deliverance from Egyptian slavery, not a political struggle. The Hebrews are portrayed as passive recipients of God's salvation rather than active political agents. Moses explicitly tells them: 'The LORD will fight for you, and you be still' (יְהוָה יִלְחַם לָכֶם וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִישׁוּן). The deliverance is effected through divine intervention—the pillar of cloud, the parting and closing of the sea—not through Hebrew military or political action. Furthermore, the geographic setting is the wilderness (מִדְבָּר), not the Hebrews' own land; they are fleeing Egypt and have not yet reached Canaan. The Egyptians, not the Hebrews, are portrayed as initiating military action, and God destroys the Egyptian forces. The emphasis is consistently on God's mighty hand (הַיָּד הַגְּדֹלָה), not on Hebrew political struggle.
